comparison: Strong agreement. Both evaluations support that HSCs are the functional source of GDF2/BMP10 (C2, C38, C39, C43). OpenEval emphasizes the systematic genetic controls and qPCR validation, while peer reviewers highlight this as a key novelty using 'state-of-the-art' approaches. Both find the evidence convincing.

Agreement on ALK1 expression. Both support claims C3 and C128 regarding ALK1 receptor expression on KCs and ECs. OpenEval focuses on flow cytometry validation from reporter mice, while peer reviewers accept this without critique as part of the overall experimental approach.

Strong agreement on KC identity loss. Both evaluations support claims C4, C35, C42, C44, C45 regarding loss of KC markers. OpenEval emphasizes immunofluorescence and flow cytometry data with appropriate controls, while peer reviewers recognize this as a novel contribution to KC differentiation/homeostasis understanding.

Agreement on KC transcriptional changes and replacement. OpenEval addresses bulk RNA-seq showing comprehensive transcriptional changes and monocyte replacement (C46-C52), while peer reviewers acknowledge the same findings (C46-C52, C56-C59) as part of the KC differentiation novelty. Both find the evidence convincing.

Agreement on MoKC differentiation block. OpenEval supports claims C53-C59 showing differentiation blocked at MoM stage using flow cytometry, while peer reviewers accept the broader finding that KCs are replaced by monocyte-derived macrophages (C56-C59 overlap). Both evaluations find this supported.

Strong agreement on EC transdifferentiation. Both evaluations support that ECs lose sinusoidal identity and gain continuous/arterial phenotypes (C70, C73-C79). OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive RNA-seq, immunofluorescence, and flow cytometry data, while peer reviewers describe findings as 'convincing' without raising concerns.

Agreement on reduced angiocrine factors. OpenEval supports claims C7, C8, C80, C81 based on RNA-seq data, while peer reviewers acknowledge reduced angiocrine factors (C8, C81) as part of downstream effects on hepatocyte function. Both find this supported.

Both uncertain/cautious about iron metabolism. OpenEval rates C9, C82 as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete penetrance (5/7 mice) and mild phenotype, while peer reviewers accept the finding (C9, C82) but note the work is 'rather descriptive.' Both acknowledge the result but with reservations about completeness.

Agreement on disrupted metabolic zonation. Both evaluations support claims C10, C83-C87 regarding loss of glutamine synthetase and Wnt target downregulation. OpenEval emphasizes the redundancy demonstrated by single knockout controls, while peer reviewers accept this as part of hepatocyte function effects.

Agreement on reduced liver size. OpenEval supports C88, C89 showing reduced liver size with quantitative data, while peer reviewers accept this (C88, C89) as part of the overall liver dysfunction phenotype without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on fibrosis phenotype. Both evaluations support claims C6, C90-C99 regarding fibrosis, HSC activation, and capillarization. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive multi-assay validation and mechanistic interpretation, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the 'convincing' demonstration of liver homeostasis disruption.

Strong agreement on overarching conclusions. Both evaluations support the integrated conclusions (C11, C100-C103, C122-C124) about HSC-mediated cell-cell crosstalk. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive experimental support, while peer reviewers explicitly endorse that 'BMP9 and BMP10 produced by HSC play a central role in mediating liver cell-cell crosstalk and liver homeostasis.'

Both acknowledge non-canonical signaling but note limitations. OpenEval supports C60-C65 showing non-overlapping DEGs beyond ALK1-Smad4, while peer reviewers note similar findings (C64-C69) but critique that 'molecular mechanisms are barely touched upon.' Both recognize the finding but peer reviewers want more mechanistic depth.

Both uncertain about Rxra mechanism. OpenEval rates C66-C69 as UNCERTAIN, noting the claim is appropriately cautious ('may be partially caused'), while peer reviewers similarly note (C66-C69) that mechanisms 'could have been more explored.' Both acknowledge the finding but consider mechanistic explanation incomplete.

Both uncertain about Stab2Cre speculation. OpenEval rates C104-C112 as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic explanations are speculative, while peer reviewers similarly critique (C62, C109-C112) that the work 'remains rather descriptive' with underdeveloped mechanisms. Both view this as informed speculation rather than demonstrated fact.

OpenEval identifies C113-C114 as UNCERTAIN speculation about HC/EC contributions to macrophage niche that is not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval identifies C115-C121 as UNCERTAIN speculation about human disease mechanisms based on mouse data, appropriately noting this as hypothesis generation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these translational speculations.

Agreement on local production importance. OpenEval supports C125-C128 emphasizing local HSC production is critical based on unchanged heart Bmp10 and weak ALK1 expression, while peer reviewers accept C128 (weak ALK1 expression) as part of the receptor expression validation without challenge.

OpenEval identifies C1, C12-C34, C40 as SUPPORTED established knowledge and prior literature providing study context. These background claims are not separately evaluated by peer reviewers, who focus on novel findings rather than literature review.

Peer reviewers evaluate C36, C102 (additional hepatocyte function claims) as SUPPORTED that are not grouped in a separate OpenEval result, though these claims appear in OpenEval R9, R11, and R14 evaluations as part of broader claim sets.
Peer reviewers evaluate C5, C37 (additional liver dysfunction claims) as SUPPORTED that are not explicitly grouped in OpenEval results, though related phenotypes are covered in OpenEval R12 and R13.
